title: He was close to glory.
paragraphs: He was close to glory.
And still wanted the throne.

“How you are fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!... For you have said in your heart: ‘I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne... I will be like the Most High.’” — Isaiah 14:12–14
This is the madness of pride.

Not just thinking highly of yourself.
Not just enjoying your gifts.
Pride is the soul saying, “God, move aside.”
Lucifer was not ruined by weakness first.
He was ruined by self-exaltation.

Five times the passage thunders with “I will.”
That is the language of rebellion.
That is creation trying to replace the Creator.
That is beauty becoming poison.
That is brilliance turning demonic.
But here’s what we miss—

Pride never looks ugly at the beginning.
It looks strong.
Confident.
Untouchable.
It glitters before it devours.

Lucifer did not fall because God was threatened.
He fell because no creature can steal a throne that belongs to the Holy One alone.
“Yet you shall be brought down to Sheol, to the lowest depths of the Pit.” — Isaiah 14:15
That is where pride always goes.
Down.
And the terrifying part is this: the same poison that destroyed Lucifer still whispers in human hearts.

“Build your own name.”
“Protect your image.”
“Sit at the center.”
“Obey no one.”

That is not freedom.
That is the ancient lie with a fresh coat of paint.
But the Gospel tells a better story.

Where Lucifer said, “I will exalt myself,” Jesus “humbled Himself” and became obedient to death—even the death of the cross (Philippians 2:8).
Where pride reached upward to seize glory, Christ came downward to save sinners.
Where rebellion brought ruin, surrender to Jesus brings life.

This is our hope:
Proud hearts can be broken.
Rebels can repent.
The arrogant can be forgiven.
Because Jesus saves not the self-crowned, but the self-surrendered.
So lay it down.

The ego.
The performance.
The silent throne in your chest.

Christ does not share His crown.
But He will gladly save the one who bows.
Pride made Lucifer fall. Grace can make you kneel—and live.
